components.gap: The Remarks qualifying Theorem 3.4.17 (Durrett p. 157) are not all supplied. Present: validity for all n and x with nontrivial content only for n >= 10 (annex 318-323) and the impossibility of a uniformly faster rate for fair signs (annex 438-448). Missing: (i) the historical claim that the constant 3 is not the best known, van Beek (1972) obtaining 0.8; (ii) the attribution of this streamlined smoothing method and its good constant to Feller (the source cites Feller's own claim that the method gives a remarkably good bound while avoiding messy numerical calculations); (iii) the mathematical claim that the hypothesis E|X|^3 < infinity is needed to obtain the rate n^{-1/2}.

defect_observations.observation: Example 4.8.10 is given as approximately 0.1084; the source prints 0.1083 (from 7.225/66.655 = 0.10839 truncated). The handbook value is the correctly rounded one; no coverage effect.

The random-index theorem applied with a_t = floor(t/mu) yields normalization sigma*sqrt(a_t); the displayed limit uses sigma*sqrt(t/mu). The deterministic factor sqrt(a_t mu/t) -> 1 (perturbation lemma) is not written explicitly. Elementary; no coverage effect recorded.
Phi(2) - Phi(-2) is given as about 0.9545; the source table value is 0.9546. Rounding only.
